To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
moderate exercise is superior to vigorous exercise in prolonging life.
1) moderate exercise is better for the cardiovascular system than vigorous exercise.

(i) moderate intensity exercise training is associated with a significant reduction of sympathetic tone and an increase of parasympathetic tone; (ii) this effect was more pronounced when the training was associated with a weight reduction programme; and (iii) this reduction was accompanied by a significant improvement of the lipid profile, a decrease in blood pressure and a decrease in body weight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise training on the cardiovascular and metabolic risk profiles of hypertensive patients with high levels of sympathetic activity.
the effects of exercise on the sympathetic system in hypertensive patients.
the study of the mechanisms by which the sympathetic nervous system influences the cardiovascular and endocrine systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best way to prevent cardiovascular disease is to adopt a healthy lifestyle, including a diet with low saturated fat content, low alcohol consumption, and regular physical activity, in order to reduce body weight and blood pressure, and to increase HDL cholesterol and fibrinolysis.
the most beneficial effect of exercise is obtained with a moderate intensity, and that this effect is obtained even with a small amount of exercise.

moderate exercise, which is more easily adopted, is more beneficial for the general population, whereas for those at higher risk of cardiovascular disease, vigorous exercise is more appropriate, but it is also more difficult to adopt and adhere to.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise training has beneficial effects in patients with cardiovascular diseases, the optimal intensity and duration of training are still a matter of controversy.
exercise training is an important part of cardiovascular rehabilitation.
the exercise intensity is not important in determining the health effects of physical activity, but the duration of exercise is the main factor in improving the health of the individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to the benefits of moderate-intensity exercise, the benefits of vigorous-intensity exercise are even greater.
the benefits of exercise are not necessarily linear with intensity.
the most effective way of improving your health is by engaging in regular physical activity.
